conclusion: The recipient gets a copy of the signed acknowledgment at the time of services. An oral explanation, business card or journal cannot replace that copy.

checkedSources.version: Illinois General Assembly current compilation of 5 ILCS 312
Illinois Notary Public Handbook, March 2026, I PUB 16.24 ADA

conclusion: The notary commission does not confer immigration legal expertise or authority to sell assistance involving legal analysis. The statute recognizes only the distinct qualifying roles it identifies.

The statute imposes personal liability for losses resulting from willfully failing to promptly forward money received for that purpose from an oath or acknowledgment customer. Bonding does not transfer ownership or provide immunity.

checkedSources.version: Illinois General Assembly current compilation of 5 ILCS 312

conclusion: Official misconduct can create liability for the notary and surety for caused damages. Obtaining the statutory bond neither eliminates the notary’s personal liability nor authorizes misconduct.

checkedSources.pinpoint: 5 ILCS 312/3-104(e), itemized fee receipts and records

conclusion: For fees accepted, provide itemized receipts and keep records, with notarial fees distinct from other charges. The duty does not wait for a lawsuit or impose cash only.
An individual’s official seal stays secure and cannot be loaned or used by the employer or substitute, regardless of trust, charge, or who purchased it.

An audio-video record is covered by the statutory restriction on selling or making associated notarial records available to unauthorized third parties. Commercial advertising alone is not a protected exception.
The notary may refuse an act without giving further explanation. Presentation of valid ID alone does not require the notary to approve the suspicious act or allow others to use the seal.

The provision targets knowingly creating, manufacturing or distributing software or hardware intended to enable unauthorized electronic notarial acts. Product license and appearance do not exempt that specified conduct.
Wrongful acquisition, concealment, damage or destruction of the technology used for an electronic signature or seal is a specifically prohibited act. The facts describe wrongful concealment.

The attorney-notary clause preserves notarial acts on documents the attorney prepared. It does not say the attorney can notarize their own signature, ignore a party conflict or skip identity requirements.

checkedSources.version: Illinois General Assembly current compilation of 5 ILCS 312

conclusion: Advertisements need to describe the actual limited notarial role and include prescribed notices where covered. A commission does not constitute state endorsement of legal advice.

checkedSources.version: Illinois General Assembly, current 5 ILCS 312 consolidation

conclusion: Corrected an assertion that the statute provides a law-firm exception to the employer journal-retention rule.

checkedSources.version: Illinois Secretary of State public guidance at access
14 Ill. Adm. Code §176.350, current JCAR copy

conclusion: The issued commission term rather than a seal typo controls actual authority. A mistaken later seal date, customer belief or employer demand does not extend the commission.
The proposed alteration of an already signed instrument and certification of its legal contents engage separate prohibitions. A charge or provider procedure cannot authorize either.
A private waiver cannot expand ordinary nonattorney authority to prepare a legal instrument. The Act’s limited attorney-notary provision is not authorization through customer consent.

checkedSources.version: Illinois General Assembly current compilation of 5 ILCS 312

conclusion: The certificate must describe a real completed notarial act following appearance and identity, and one cannot pre-sign the blank form. Equipment and employer approval do not supply the ceremony.

checkedSources.version: Illinois General Assembly current compilation of 5 ILCS 312

conclusion: An ordinary seal image or vendor account cannot confer the necessary electronic appointment. The electronic seal procedure requires the separate state commission and approved technology.

The authorized electronic notary must be physically in Illinois while performing the remote act. A Michigan location cannot be cured by venue language, a customer’s Illinois address, or vendor settings.

checkedSources.version: Illinois General Assembly current compilation of 5 ILCS 312

conclusion: The remote electronic venue is the real Illinois jurisdiction of the notary. Peoria County is the stated location regardless of the other state where the remote signer sits.

checkedSources.version: Illinois General Assembly current compilation of 5 ILCS 312
Illinois Notary Public Handbook, March 2026, I PUB 16.24 ADA

conclusion: For a principal abroad, the record must meet a specified U.S. filing or matter, property, or substantial transaction nexus. Currency or the presence of an application does not supply such a nexus.

Before using audio-video for an electronic act, tell all participating people that the event will be electronically recorded. The recording supplements rather than replaces the required journal record.
At least seven years of retention applies to the recording even when the electronic act was not completed. No one-day or payment-based deletion is authorized by the stated provision.

When relying on personal knowledge for electronic identity, the recording states how the notary knows the particular signer and for how long. A name or private number does not explain that relationship.

checkedSources.version: Illinois General Assembly current compilation of 5 ILCS 312
Illinois Notary Public Handbook, March 2026, I PUB 16.24 ADA

conclusion: Illinois electronic audio-video must allow simultaneous seeing and speaking, real-time signal and recording. Prerecorded messages or a later telephone call cannot supply that contemporaneous link.
When the participant exits before identity verification completes, the current rule requires restarting that identity verification process from the beginning.

checkedSources.version: Illinois General Assembly current compilation of 5 ILCS 312
Illinois Notary Public Handbook, March 2026, I PUB 16.24 ADA

conclusion: The stated electronic credential path requires photo/signed credential presentation, front-and-back analysis, and dynamic authentication. A mere image alone omits multiple required components.
The notary must visually compare the remote presenter to the analyzed credential. Automated checks are supplementary steps and a clear mismatch remains unresolved despite a software pass.
The state’s prescribed dynamic identity quiz uses at least five questions relating to history or identity. One to four questions would not meet its minimum.
Each verification quiz question has a minimum of five answer choices. A binary or yes/no response format fails this requirement.
The authentication quiz requires at least 80% correct. The scenario’s 60% does not pass; neither universal perfection nor a discretionary after-the-fact threshold is prescribed.
All identity quiz questions must be answered within two minutes. The three-hour portion relates to notary course instruction, not this remote identity assessment.

After the first failure, allow one retake within twenty-four hours, with at least 40% of the prior questions replaced. Unlimited identical retries and a complete prohibition are both inconsistent with this rule.
A second failed attempt prevents retrying with the same electronic notary within twenty-four hours. The notary cannot view or record the operator’s quiz questions and answers.

Design the identity assessment so the electronic notary cannot see or record quiz questions or answers. Coaching or placing answers in the journal would contradict the independent verification safeguard.

checkedSources.version: Illinois General Assembly current compilation of 5 ILCS 312

conclusion: After completion, both electronic seal and signature must be independently verifiable, and the association and document must make tampering evident. An editable seal image alone fails that standard.

checkedSources.version: Illinois General Assembly current compilation of 5 ILCS 312

conclusion: The electronic notary keeps exclusive control over credentials and cannot let coworkers use the electronic seal or signature. Training or managerial status does not authorize such sharing.

checkedSources.version: Illinois General Assembly, current 5 ILCS 312 consolidation
Illinois SOS Notary Public Handbook, March 2026 I PUB 16.24

conclusion: The Act describes the triggering event, not a discovery-based extension. The stem now makes occurrence and awareness contemporaneous, with the same knowledge point and answer letter.
If the remote paper audio-video link breaks, restart the remote act from the beginning and reconfirm identity. Voice-only continuation or a frozen frame cannot complete this interrupted proceeding.

The signer sends a legible copy of the entire signed record directly to the notary no later than the day after signing using a permitted delivery method. An isolated signature page two days later fails both elements.
The notary signs the transmitted copy as witness and returns it directly to the signer through permitted transmission within twenty-four hours of receipt; an unsigned receipt is insufficient.

An otherwise valid remote paper certificate states that audio-video communication was used in the form given or a substantially similar statement. A vendor number or a visible symbol does not communicate the required wording.

A single current state license with face and signature meets the documentary route. Its use does not establish personal knowledge and does not require two IDs or a passport.

The current state credential has a face photo plus physical description. The statute accepts that combination without a signature and imposes neither handwriting nor a photo-free alternative.

A federally recognized tribal government agency may issue the described current face-photo/signature ID. North Carolina issuance, the notary’s tribal membership and witness countersignature are not required.

The long relationship and elimination of reasonable doubt satisfy personal knowledge. An ID is not invariably required; employment standing and transaction value alone do not meet the test.
Brief conversation and a self-presented card are not proof of sufficient interactions to eliminate reasonable doubt on these facts. The principal cannot waive the statutory standard.

The disinterested reliable neighbor knows both necessary persons and must identify the traveler by oath or affirmation. Contact details, self-testimony and a share of proceeds do not meet this witness route.
A proposed identity witness must be personally known to the notary. Excellent ID, multiple unfamiliar witnesses and a fee waiver do not supply the statutory relationship.
The buyer’s party status independently defeats credible-witness eligibility. Age alone, familiarity and payment cannot remove that conflict.

Name-tag recognition does not substitute for the identity witness’s personal knowledge of the signer. The notary’s friend may qualify if otherwise eligible, and signer residency does not supply familiarity.
Known dishonesty about identity defeats the required reliability judgment despite no financial interest. An oath or the principal’s designation cannot cure the defect.
Ordinary in-person acknowledgment of the absent signer cannot be performed through the courier. Courier credentials, copying quality and seal size do not establish physical personal appearance.
The accessible counter meets the described physical proximity, free communication, visibility and paper exchange criteria. No private office, side of counter or table dimensions are mandated.
The act occurred in the principal’s presence, so timely truthful completion of the certificate can follow departure. This exception does not permit an absent act or false date.

The appearing subscribing witness needs personal knowledge or satisfactory evidence before proceeding. Neither witness status, their signature alone nor the question of absent principal identity removes that requirement.

Face photograph and issuer are insufficient without signature or physical description. Short record and categorical ban on government IDs both misstate the rule.

One fully qualified credible witness can establish satisfactory evidence by sworn or affirmed identification. No second witness is generally needed for this identity route and the witness cannot sign as principal.

A certificate cannot be made or given without personal knowledge or satisfactory evidence of the requisite identity. A printed name, recipient check or later delivery follow-up does not meet the prerequisite.

Receiving proceeds makes the proposed witness a beneficiary even if reliable and personally known. The oath and lack of a principal objection do not cure, and the record is not categorically barred merely because it is a settlement.
Observed signing is a separate part of acknowledgment and cannot alone satisfy the identity requirement. A coworker watching or rendering free service does not change that duty.

The oral affirmation still requires personal appearance and qualifying identity in the traditional scenario, plus the vow of truthfulness. A signature is not invariably required, and the recipient cannot replace the notary’s determination.
Long familiarity addresses identity alone. For this traditional acknowledgment the coworker messenger and text message do not establish physical appearance, or remove certification duties.

A current otherwise qualifying federal agency credential with facial photograph and physical description is covered. Vehicle agencies do not have exclusive authority; a generic federal letter or private logo badge is insufficient.
The grantee is a party to the deed transaction and cannot provide this disinterested proof. Proper identification, a grantor photo and a waived fee do not eliminate party status.

Credible witness role is identity, while a subscribing witness signs to witness execution or acknowledgment and can give a qualifying proof. Recognizing a name or signing as the principal does not suffice.
The principal in a proof is the individual whose execution or signature is being established, distinct from the subscribing witness. Fee payer and employed-by labels cannot select the principal.
The notary must establish a valid identity route before acting or making the certificate. Employment instructions, initials and a risk surcharge cannot displace that prohibition.
An appearing, identified homeowner may acknowledge her existing signature. Observed signing is an alternative, and neither backdating nor a neighbor’s accuracy testimony is part of this route.
Personal observation in physical presence satisfies the signature element when the other requirements are present. It does not administer an oath, waive ID or certify a copy.
A denied signature cannot be truthfully acknowledged. Identity match, recipient acceptance and recasting an unobserved signature as observed do not cure that issue.
Acknowledgment establishes appearance, identity and the signature element. It does not alone administer a truth vow, validate substantive enforceability or support a jurat’s unperformed oath.
An appearing and identified person’s truth vow on penalty of perjury using swear fits the oath definition. It is not a signature acknowledgment, seal registration or unsworn proof.
The personal-honor truth vow without deity or swear is an affirmation equivalent to an oath. It can support a jurat, does not become an acknowledgment and needs no religious language.
Both statutory acts entail truthfulness on penalty of perjury; the distinction concerns the vow’s phrasing. Neither informal conversation nor signature alone supplies either.
An oral oath may be administered without a jurat; notarizing a signature needs a certificate. A signed affidavit or second notary is not required here, and the act is within statutory authority.
Jurat evidences administration of oath or affirmation. It does not prove actual truth or government warranty, and it has no commissioning function.
Jurat describes the signed record and actual sworn or affirmed truth statement. A heading, seal or out-of-county use does not effect an omitted oath.

Identified, disinterested subscribing witness who personally observed signing may give proof by sworn testimony. It is not absent-principal acknowledgment or copy certification, and identification still applies.
Subscribed witness to the principal’s own acknowledgment can give qualifying sworn proof despite not seeing original signing. Unsworn or beneficiary testimony is not allowed.

A disinterested identified nonsubscribing witness may recognize the principal signature as genuine under oath or affirmation. Notary conjecture and relabeling the witness as principal do not meet the proof requirements.
The genuine-signature recognition route also covers the subscribing witness’s signature. The sworn genuineness statement and appearing witness identification remain essential.
Refusing both oath and affirmation defeats this proof even if testimony otherwise fits. Principal return, witness seal or copy of the record does not supply the required oath.
Observation alone does not make a person a subscribing witness: signing the record for that role is essential. Being a notary or simply receiving a copy is not the test.
The signature-by-mark route requires witnessed affixation, prescribed notation and an authorized notarization. Stamping alone, adding later by an employee and a cursive-only rule do not comply.
The prescribed text identifies the signer and that the mark was placed in the undersigned notary’s presence. Choice of transaction, literacy and fee are not notation contents.
The mark must be affixed in the notary’s presence for this procedure. A relative’s statement, backdating and recipient waiver do not substitute for it.

The physically unable principal may direct a disinterested designee using the full statutory procedure. No unrequested notary signature, interested buyer without witnesses or blank execution suffices.
The principal must personally direct the designee to sign before the notary and two unaffected witnesses. Facility selection and a relative or recipient acting alone do not supply that direction.

Both direction and signing require two unaffected witnesses; the absent second one is the missing person. Principal agreement, an interested beneficiary or later remote promise cannot replace their attendance.
Designee signs the principal’s name before the principal, notary and witnesses. Using the designee, certifier or recipient name is not the prescribed execution.
Both witnesses sign their own names on the record near the principal signature. Attendance, signing the notary name and signing only an envelope do not satisfy the requirement.
The required below-signature statement identifies names and addresses of principal and witnesses. Designee ID number, marketing text and purchase amount omit required data.
The final required step is an authorized notarization beyond execution, witness signing and notation. These steps do not themselves notarize, and designee signatures are permitted when compliant.
The purchaser receiving the property is not a disinterested designee. Ability to write, principal waiver and fee payment do not eliminate the transaction interest.
The cited subdivision authorizes the three stated notarial-act families. It confers no general appraisal, transaction guarantee or dispute-resolution power.
Notary cannot authenticate the photograph itself but may notarize an attached affidavit about it. Stamping it, waiving a fee or asserting state guarantee does not authorize photo authentication.
The sworn affidavit’s formalities are the subject of the resulting act. It does not establish authenticity of the image, copyright ownership or camera settings.

Attestation is completing the certificate after the notarial act has been performed. It neither substitutes for the act, drafts the transaction record nor requires the recipient to sign the official seal.
The chosen act’s statutory elements are certified by making the certificate even when not written out. Omitted recitals, recipient-drafted wording and short form do not eliminate that duty.

A truth vow on penalty of perjury invoking deity satisfies the oath wording alternative without swear. Religious wording is allowed and the underlying truth vow remains required.

The stamped image must appear clear and legible. A blur, initials or invoice cannot satisfy this duty even if a separate preservation rule can protect the certificate.
On paper, both official signature and seal must appear on the same page as certificate text. Neither same envelope, seal-only placement nor recipient preference meets the standard.
The venue follows the actual place of acknowledgment in Durham. The commissioning seal county, property’s situs and lender preference do not establish the venue.
Thursday is the true act date even though Monday is the earlier signing date. Closing approvals and filing deadlines cannot supply or change the certificate date.
Certify only the actual appearing principal who acknowledged, as identified or clear in the record. An earlier signature, fee payer or co-owner consent is not the absent person’s appearance.
A signature notarization requires a certificate identifying the performed act. A seal, page count and payment mark do not provide that identification.

Capacity and identity method are permitted additions to an otherwise sufficient certificate. Judicial authorship is not required and false facts remain prohibited.

The appearing principal’s name need not be separately listed where already clear from the record. That does not dispense with identification or permit a recipient name; the rule specifically concerns the principal.

The certificate dates today’s actual oath/affirmation. Drafting last month, commission date and future filing do not establish the date of the act.
Lawful nonexpired and unsuspended commission is certified both at act and at certificate signature. Application date, recipient consent and backdating do not cure lapse at signing.
A traditional act across state lines is outside a North Carolina-only commission. Origination, residence and seal do not alter jurisdiction; the certificate implies lawful geographic limits.

Where the principal appears unable to understand the transaction’s nature or consequences, statutory certification cannot be made. Identity, companion authorization and not reading the form cannot cure the assessment.

The stated threat creates apparent involuntariness and duress, which the acknowledgment implied certification cannot truthfully deny. Passage of signing, companion waiver or payment does not resolve this.
A suspended commission cannot support the required certification despite a future expiration date. Free service, operating seal and date alone cannot restore authority.
An erroneous expiration statement does not harm the certificate or related record when the notary was actually commissioned at the act. It does not legalize an actual lapse or other false statements.

Paper certificate requires the notary’s own handwritten ink signature after the act. A scan, delegated printing and principal signing cannot replace it regardless of use of a genuine seal.
Borrower personally signed the record and is disqualified. Fee waiver, repeat stamping and self-knowledge do not override signer status.
Purchaser remains a party even when notarizing only the other party’s signature. Seller consent, ink color and avoidance of self-signature do not cure party status.

A sole authorized drafter can come within the exception, without granting drafting authority or relaxing appearance. Drafter designation does not invariably mean beneficiary.

Attorney-for-one-party designation alone is excepted if there is no other individual, representative or fiduciary party role. It confers neither blanket immunity nor self-signature authority.

Nonreceipt of the original with a request within 60 days of issuance qualifies for a free duplicate. Neither the bond amount, mandatory training nor refusing all duplicates applies.
The resignation facts require state notification and destruction. Continuing until the stamp fails, notifying only clients and transferring the stamp are incorrect.
Domestic partnership itself disqualifies. The nature of the record, witness or lack of a fee cannot lift this restriction.
The partner's parent is among the listed relations. The rule extends outside blood and wills, and partner permission does not remove it.
The adopted child of a sibling falls expressly within the definition. The restriction is neither limited to direct children nor limited to natural-born relatives.

The short form requires the notary to sign the certificate. Neither another photocopy nor customer email completes that signature.
Customer possession does not change a source record’s public classification. The statutory exclusion controls regardless of label, value or folder.
Verify actual accuracy and absence of alteration before certifying true and exact reproduction. Appearance, payment and acceptance by another jurisdiction do not verify it.

conclusion: For a new ordinary term, the published procedure requires another RON application. Prior certification and functioning old credentials do not carry forward.
The remote notary must be physically present in Utah. Client, provider server and billing locations do not establish that fact.
Clear audio alone cannot satisfy live simultaneous sight and sound with an unfamiliar signer. A still image or recorded performance does not restore live interaction.
When using an ID image for the remote procedure, it must be clear enough to establish satisfactory identity. A price or verbal statement cannot make a blurry credential useful.
Each RON act needs its audiovisual recording, with security for nonpublic data. The key does not depend on the erroneous §46-1-41.1 cross-reference in §46-1-3.6(3)(a).
A lawfully performed RON satisfies state-law personal appearance for that act. It does not substitute a vendor presence, require a later trip, or waive all future appearances.
In the unfamiliar-signer qualifying ID route, secondary authentication supplements initial documentation. Payment and unrelated evidence do not authenticate the correct signer.
Facial recognition may be biometric secondary authentication when compliant. It is a distinct category from administration, copying and fees.
Third-party dynamic questions using personal information from public or proprietary sources constitute knowledge-based secondary authentication, distinct from a document oath or the exam.

The statutory definition makes secondary authentication apply to the unknown witness, but a separately worded principal-ID requirement in §46-1-3.6(2)(b) must be addressed. Scope the question expressly to whose identity the secondary-authentication definition addresses, without teaching that the witness bypasses principal requirements.
The RON certificate must state that the notarization was performed remotely. An absent-appearance claim, advertising or enforceability guarantee does not meet the requirement.
Attachment of electronic certificate signature and seal must reveal later changes to the certificate or associated record. A replaceable seal image without evidence fails that condition.
Utah requires the remote seal rendered black. Purple is the in-person ink rule and client preferences are immaterial.
The electronic seal is ordinarily accessible only to its guardian and named remote notary. Limited authorized purposes do not allow customer or general vendor access.
Only the named remote notary may use the electronic seal to perform the act. Technical assistance or limited guardian access does not appoint a substitute notary.

The written certification is of credential destruction within ten days. The original stem says the former notary disabled credentials, which may improperly imply disabling suffices; revise to say statutory destruction occurred.
Resignation triggers destruction of credentials enabling official signing or sealing. Personal authority cannot transfer or remain available for free or emergency acts.
The business exception is limited to creating, obtaining or possessing electronic seals for provision to certified notaries. It does not confer authority to notarize or displace seal standards.
The notary cannot promote a product through the official title or seal. Color, payment, truth of the ad or customer consent do not make official endorsement permissible.
The special required modified-message rule applies to qualifying non-English advertising. The original only says radio and omits this premise, so the requirement cannot be asserted categorically.

The $10 cap for each immigration-status form set per individual applies regardless of acting as a notary. The licensed attorney professional-services exception does not apply. The fee ceiling gives no authority to provide legal advice.
The licensed escrow agent/title insurance producer exception may apply under the stated role and naming restrictions. It does not waive independent disqualifications or identification.
The statute expressly cross-references self-proved paper and electronic will exceptions. The specified probate conditions still apply, and simply labeling a will does not create a blanket exception.
A lawful narrowly scoped court order is an express authorized guardian access/use purpose. It does not transfer the commission or authorize ongoing unrelated acts.
For this nonremote qualifying plat, permanent-ink signature plus exact commissioned name and number, Utah notary wording and expiration next to or below it can satisfy the imprint exception.
The physical map-or-plat exception text expressly excludes a certificate completed through remote notarization. Property ownership and vendor approval do not enlarge it.
The notary timely supplies official name-change proof and bond rider reflecting both names to the lieutenant governor within 30 days. Other announcements do not amend the state record.
The name-change process directs destruction of both original commission and obsolete seal. Neither can be transferred or used in parallel.
Utah expressly does not require adoption of a spouse’s surname. Marriage by itself does not end the commission or transfer the seal.
The 30-day notice applies to either residential or business address change. Report the new business address to the lieutenant governor even if home is unchanged.
The lieutenant governor receives the resignation notice identifying its effective date. Vendor closure or payment issues do not establish that date.

Discovery of statutory unlawful interference requires immediately notifying law enforcement with jurisdiction and giving the lieutenant governor written notice. Employer notification alone is insufficient.
Accidental destruction still triggers immediate written notice to the lieutenant governor. A criminal suspect, fraudulent use or replacement order is not a precondition.

checkedSources.version: Current Utah Code consolidation; S.B. 139, 2026 Ch. 56

conclusion: The required written notice includes the time period covered by affected journals or recordings. An appointment or equipment price does not identify the statutory scope.

Email to the official published address is an express permitted route, along with certified mail or another delivery with a confirmed receipt. A signer message or forum comment is not adequate notice.
The definition recognizes authority granted for specific maintenance, repair or technical support. Proper authorization matters, without permitting falsification or transferring journal ownership.
A compliance agreement and applicant email must accompany the application. A name and bond do not supply those missing statutory fields.
The statutory review requires an applicant-signed waiver on the office’s form. A private prior background check or a customer consent is not the statutory waiver.
Solicitation of a notary-chapter violation by the employer may be a class B misdemeanor if not another criminal offense. The manager’s request does not confer authority.
The lieutenant governor may suspend or revoke on a ground permitting denial of an application. The act is discretionary, independent of customers and vendors.
A chapter violation alone does not invalidate notice to third parties of the document's contents. This does not validate the entire transaction or excuse violations.
The statute permits application denial for official notarial misconduct even after a passing score. Convictions are only one category of grounds.
Additional coverage runs from certification effective date to ordinary commission expiry. There is no new four-year cycle, single-appointment period or vendor billing standard.

The specified electronic-message details are exact commissioned name and number plus notary public, state and expiration wording. The explanation preserves other applicable electronic/remote requirement checks.
A currently commissioned applicant uses the name from the ordinary commission rather than customer name, brand or unlisted nickname.

conclusion: The applicant completes and notarizes the oath before filling in the application, then uploads it. Renewal, a first act and an employer request do not set the timing.

The applicable Vermont-licensed attorney in good standing is exempt from the base jurisprudence exam and base-renewal continuing education. Application, notarial law and any Special Endorsement obligations remain.

The government-issued driver license expired two years ago falls within the listed no-more-than-three-years window if identification is otherwise satisfactory. A private membership card and unrestricted age do not qualify.
Unresolved coercion is a basis to refuse. The companion’s approval, identification and payment do not establish the signer’s knowing and voluntary choice.
A signer who will not personally appear by a lawful method cannot acknowledge through a courier. The courier’s identity, copied ID and proximity do not supply the absent signer’s appearance.

For ordinary tangible-record work, the stamp alternative is clearly printed/typed name and commission number, while the assumed other certificate requirements include signature and expiration. A logo or borrowed stamp cannot identify this officer.
The ordinary commissioned notary needs OPR’s Special Endorsement for electronic-record or remote acts. Email, paying for a stamp and signer consent do not supply authority.

The ordinary nonexempt commission without specialty requires one approved CE hour completed before applying to renew. No blanket exemption, ten hours or post-approval course is specified. The optional endorsement has a separate additional course requirement. The dated exam’s inconsistent CE prompt does not override the renewal instructions or rule.
The officer must physically be in Vermont while performing the remote notarial act. Signer address, platform headquarters and client consent do not extend Vermont authority to Massachusetts.
File through OPR's Online Services System. Supplier, private learning site and employee files do not submit the commission application.

checkedSources.pinpoint: Apply by Registration, oath bullet, p. 1

conclusion: Upload a scanned completed, signed and notarized oath. Reusing an unsigned copy or adding photos or bookings leaves it incomplete.
Application completeness includes required attestations as well as answers, documentation, materials and fees. Seal ownership and coworker endorsement do not replace attestations.
The Office may deem a commission or endorsement application expired after six months incomplete. The period does not guarantee appointment or entitlement to an endorsement.
OPR may refuse a redundant application while the original is in process or after denial. Filing twice neither waives requirements nor creates transferable authority.

After a certified-mail notice of intended denial on these grounds, the applicant has 30 days to seek a hearing before an Administrative Law Officer. That right does not dispense with approval or confer provisional practice.
The OPR website accepts an unauthorized-practice complaint. Customers, a prep service and supply stores do not administer the state process.

The Director does not grant routine waivers without amending the rule. The written extraordinary-circumstance mechanism is distinct from inordinate inconvenience, customer consent and employer permission.
The initial applicant must satisfy the 18-year minimum. Finishing study and employment do not lower it, and the customer's age is a separate issue.
The initial applicant must be a US citizen or permanent legal resident. Connectivity, stamps and free services do not fulfill that particular status requirement.

Actual practice in Vermont may supply the qualifying state connection for a New Hampshire resident. Customers alone do not necessarily establish a place of practice, and Vermont residence is not the only route.
The ordinary nonexempt applicant passes the Office-approved basic exam. Business experience, an employer interview and stamp purchase are not substitutes.
Execute and submit the oath before commission issuance. First service, future renewal and an employer promise cannot replace it.
A pending applicant cannot advertise words or insignia implying they already hold notary authority. Business cards and a private disclaimer do not create the commission.
Suspended or revoked officers may not perform or attempt a notarial act. An employer, clear stamp or gratuitous favor does not restore authority.
The notary commission does not authorize legal drafting, advice or practice. Past customers, no fee and immigration subject matter do not enlarge that authority.
Absent other legal permission, the notary cannot withhold the original provided for service. Receiving the item or disputing a fee does not transfer title or automatically establish a lien.
Under the Vermont commission an ordinary act must occur while the notary is physically within Vermont. Destination, mailing address and stamp ownership do not relocate the notary.
Sign using the same name as on the submitted notarized oath. An employer identity, optional stamp and office nickname do not fulfill the signature requirement.
Report an email, address or name change in the online file within 30 days. Renewal and undeliverable email are not the triggering events.

conclusion: Submit the revised notarized oath and required supporting name documentation before acting following a name change. Customer recognition, readable stamp and social updates do not qualify the new signature.
Dishonest application misstatement is a potential basis for denial or other listed action. Payment, a vendor notice or employer benefit does not remove that basis.
Other-state suspension and listed actions are grounds Vermont may consider. They do not enlarge Vermont authority or delegate the decision to suppliers.
The electronic public database verifies authority and indicates electronic-record notification status. Neither ratings, receipts nor calendars do so.
The judiciary employee in this covered official role still must obtain a commission. Being a government employee, free service and the initial term do not waive it.
The rule lists exam, fee and base-renewal continuing education for the qualifying judiciary category. It does not confer a special-endorsement waiver or remove all law.
The official-duty exemptions do not cover unrelated private appointments. All generally applicable law and rules—including ordinary identity checks—apply to those acts.
Vermont-licensed attorneys in good standing have exam and base-renewal CE exemptions. Filing, applicable fees, ordinary act duties and any specialist conditions remain.
The applicant needs Vermont attorney admission and good standing to claim this exemption. Another state's admission, a study promise, stationery and record possession do not add that Vermont status.
The town-clerk assistant’s specified exemption is the ordinary fee. It does not waive applications, technology requirements or active authorization.
The justice of the peace is fee exempt under this provision. It does not waive identity duties, application attestations or commissioning.
A qualifying law-enforcement-related employee needs neither credential for specified official-duty work. It grants neither private-work exemption nor foreign authority.
The ordinary judiciary exemption does not automatically confer the Special Endorsement. Fee waiver, short documents and a customer's tablet do not establish it.
The ordinary attorney exam exemption does not itself supply electronic/remote authorization. The Special Endorsement remains, regardless of law school or signature image.
OPR refers a complaint involving a Vermont-licensed attorney to the Professional Responsibility Board and requests the final disposition. Dismissal, a refund and a supply store do not satisfy it.
The specified town-clerk statutory provision describes the clerk’s county. Neither a document destination, worldwide reach nor one town-hall desk sets that scope.
A record necessary to protect the public or property is among the statutory official-duty criteria. Favor, fee and paper color do not independently qualify.
The section expressly preserves unauthorized-practice prosecution under 3 V.S.A. § 127. It neither guarantees immunity nor reduces enforcement to warnings nor permits invented exceptions.
For conflicting statutory and rule standards of unprofessional conduct, apply the standard most protective of the public. Customer, employer and convenience are not the criteria.
Seek a declaratory ruling under 3 V.S.A. § 808 and OPR procedure. Contract notes, a poll and vendor promises do not invoke that state route.
The commission gives no immunity or benefit reserved by Vermont law for public officers or employees. An automatic liability waiver or transfer to a supplier does not follow.
The ordinary commission issuance charge is $30, with separate exemptions as applicable. It is not per client signature, universally free or vendor-set.

A familiar face without sufficient dealings for reasonable certainty does not establish personal knowledge. Use an adequate statutory identity route, not signature alone or the customer's consent to omit it.
The license can qualify two years after expiration. The outer date is three years before the act, not the officer’s commission date or an unlimited period.
A passport expired four years ago falls outside the stated documentary evidence window. Use another lawful method, since travel markings and fees do not extend expiration.
The other government ID category requires a signature or photograph, timeliness and officer satisfaction. Two features together are not mandatory and a private club logo is not enough.
The other-government ID still must satisfy the officer after timing and feature tests. A review threat, government label and discouraging additional inquiry do not compel acceptance.
The officer can request necessary additional information or credentials to assure identity. Fees, an unsigned promise and refusing to consider more evidence do not resolve it.
A credible witness appearing in person may be identified by the stated current license rather than by acquaintance. A private membership card or skipping witness identification does not qualify.
Email alone does not meet personal appearance or sworn/affirmed verification. Payment, confidence and an extra emailed signature do not supply either condition.
The listed witness credential is current or expired no more than three years. One year is within range without requiring same-day issuance, and neither a ten-year window nor an expiry ban applies.
The person making the statement or signing must personally appear via an authorized route. A prepaid fee, original ink and courier attendance cannot substitute.
The ordinary physical paper procedure requires the person and notary together in the same physical space. Telephone, courier and email do not do so.
The officer may refuse when competence or capacity remains unsatisfactory subject to other law. A relative, payment and an employer statement do not supply the individual's capacity.
Pressure is relevant to whether the signature is knowingly and voluntarily made. Document appearance, referrals and the companion’s haste are irrelevant.
Other law can prohibit refusal. Employer preference, an asserted blanket right and customer payment cannot override the governing rule.
A representative states proper authority and execution as the represented person’s act. The acknowledgment does not guarantee debt, profits or authorship.
An agent or attorney-in-fact is acting in representative capacity. This does not automatically confer bar status, commission the principal or turn the act into copy certification.
Beyond identification of the appearing person, the officer needs confirmation that the record contains that person’s signature. Stamp color and cost do not address the denial.
Verification requires the person's solemn declaration that the record statement is true. Account setup, a signature-style choice and paper condition do not provide it.
The officer determines the appearing affiant's identity and that the statement signature is theirs. Seal fit, document familiarity and cash are irrelevant.
Attestation concerns the identified individual appearing and signing the record. Mailing details, destination and retrospective witnessing do not supply signing before the officer.
The spouse’s party status prohibits the act even when the officer is unnamed. Free service and electronic form do not alter the conflict.
The unnamed officer’s direct beneficial interest independently triggers the conflict provision. Consent, the absence of a name and looking only at a spouse’s interest cannot remove it.
Violation makes the act voidable. It is not forgiven by performance, does not grant immunity and leaves possible legal challenge.
The described general Vermont copy certification covers a tangible copy of an electronic source. Ordinary paper-to-paper copies are outside that rule even when private or vendor-endorsed.
The notary reasonably determines whether the source electronic record is in a tamper-evident format. PDF extension, printer make and signature count do not answer that question.
The notary personally prints the electronic record or supervises printing to a tangible medium. Customer assurances, a premature seal and private courier certification do not supply it.
Do not certify once an electronic signature or record information change/error is identified. Appearance, deleting the signature and a fee cannot cure that detection.
A recorder may accept a qualifying accurately certified tangible copy for the original-record requirement. This neither mandates every printout nor supersedes all recording law or guarantees title.
The physically unable individual may direct someone other than the notary to sign the individual's name. The notary cannot be the proxy, and stamp purchase is unrelated.
Insert the required or equivalent statement naming who signed and who directed the signing. Omission, job title and wrongly claiming the notary signed for the person do not accurately document it.
Remote location alone does not support proxy signing due to physical inability. A free fee or using the notary as the proxy does not expand the exception.
The timing is contemporaneous with actual performance, with no notary presignature. Recipient choice, supplies and renewal do not establish the actual date.
Perform the act before attaching or associating the notary signature. Early payment, expensive paper and a customer's signature cannot authorize presigning.
State the actual notarial date and performance jurisdiction. Destination, lawyer address, payment timing and birthplace do not determine them.
The office title and commission expiration are required along with the signature. Customer occupation, tax value and signature alone do not supply them.
The certificate must be part of or securely attached to its tangible record. Loose pages, later oral promises and email do not make the required connection.
The electronic certificate is affixed to or logically associated with its record. Discarding it, advertising and unrelated storage do not evidence the electronic act.
When the certificate is on a page other than the individual’s name and signature, include the individual's name on the certificate. Printer model, parking code and blank page count do not substitute.
The short form identifies the representative authority type and actual represented party. Property predictions, personal preferences and a liability guarantee are unrelated.
The verification short form documents that the named individual signed and affirmed before the notary. Delivery, payment or business endorsement does not describe the act.
The ordinary paper certificate may use required printed/typed identification instead of a purchased physical stamp. Other fields remain necessary and an employer cannot decide to omit them.

A stampless paper certificate prints or types the name, number and commission expiration along with the remaining required information. Nicknames, icons and unrelated customer details do not substitute.
The Vermont State Seal is forbidden on the official physical stamp. It is neither a required design nor a substitute for the commission number, regardless of client approval.
Embossers and ink stamps must be reproducible with the record. Cost, a second non-reproducible impression and device type do not exempt it.
The commission number is minimum physical stamp content alongside name, Vermont and Notary Public title. A map or customer signature is not a substitute.
Print/type any required certificate information that is not on the optional stamp. Assuming or omitting the field fails even with an otherwise valid impression.

Once the stamp’s printed expiration date has passed, use an updated/no-expiration stamp or discontinue physical stamping. Reusing obsolete details, erasing the required number or handing it to a customer are not the choices.
Device control and no other individual's use include a commissioned coworker. Commission, manager permission, and scheduling do not authorize borrowing.
Prompt notice to OPR, with a 48-hour outside limit after discovery, is the physical-stamp requirement. A vendor, actual misuse, and renewal are inapposite.

Proven active authority when the acknowledgment was taken preserves validity despite an inaccurate or expired listed date. No permission to use wrong dates, restore an expired commission, or cure other defects follows.
The original notary makes a corrective writing under oath before a different notary and it takes effect upon recording. Edits by the recipient, self-oath, and a stamp vendor are not this procedure.
Validity-saving language cannot validate a purported act by a person lacking authority. A stamp image and recipient approval cannot supply it.
An aggrieved person can still challenge the underlying transaction or record and seek other state or federal remedies. An acknowledgment does not determine fairness or confer blanket immunity.
An ordinary commission alone cannot cover the electronic record even with the signer in the room. Hardware and consent cannot supply a special endorsement.
An authorized remote act may use a tangible or electronic record under its applicable procedures. Paper does not eliminate the endorsement or certificate.
A special endorsement applicant must hold an active commission in good standing. Internet access and references do not replace status.
Tamper-evidence and identity-proofing attestations are separate from the communications technology attestation. Stamp receipts, assumptions, and sales claims are not adequate.
The nonexempt issuance fee is $30 as a separate statutory endorsement charge. It is neither set by customers, based on duration, nor universally waived.
The notary selects tamper-evident technology and may decline requests to use an unselected system. Customer choice, logos, or upload do not compel adoption.
Selected technology must support independent signature verification and reveal later alterations to the electronic record. Background appearance, fees, and a stapler do not achieve either.
Technology must use a valid digital certificate from a third-party provider. A review, stamp catalog, or self-created image does not supply it.
The notary cannot use an expired digital certificate, independently of commission expiration. Waiving payment or getting consent does not cure validity.
Issuer revocation independently bars use even before the digital credential's printed expiry. Sales or customer acts cannot restore it.

The electronic certificate must indicate that the act was performed electronically on an electronic record. Neither worldwide acceptance wording nor device branding or iconography states the required fact.

The notary uses the digital certificate for a verifiable signature association, and the notarial certificate must be affixed to or logically associated with the electronic record. Rule 7-2(d)'s indexed line is incomplete, but its visible opening and adjacent binding provisions establish the answer. Customer pasting, a phone number, and unrelated storage fail.

Use the same electronic signature across acts and submit a copy to OPR. The signature is unique to that notary. Vendor sharing, customer inventing it, and asserting that OPR cannot receive it are incorrect.
A signature is unique and stays under its notary's sole control/access. Employer or branch ownership, other commissions, and a common password do not allow shared use.
The notary retains control of the security aspects, including the token, credentials, and PIN. A coworker independently performing acts, customer control, or public posting fails.

Precautions govern disclosure to document preparation/transmission vendors, while the notary retains security control. The rule also names OPR/designee requests and judicial subpoena, and does not authorize vendor notarization or credential ownership.

Expiration of either the commission or endorsement triggers destruction and disabling of the enabling electronic signature and any electronic stamp credentials. Size, subscription date, or transfer cannot supersede it.
Theft of the digital certificate requires immediate office notice. The physical tool's distinct 48-hour outside limit, renewal, and a customer loss threshold are inapplicable.
Dealings yielding reasonable certainty can satisfy identity through personal knowledge. KBA is not also required for this route, while preferred names or no determination cannot substitute.
Without personal knowledge or credible witness the rule requires both types, credential analysis and dynamic KBA. Payment, photograph alone, or only one tool fails.
Reasonable confirmation of the same signed or addressed record is required. Style, filename similarity and payment cannot resolve differing pages.

If the tangible record is before the notary, recorded display of the record and remote signer's identification is the recognized acknowledgment method. An envelope, later view of desk, or unrelated coworker cannot replace it.
While on the audiovisual recording the signer signs both the record and declaration, incorporated into or securely attached to the record. Envelope, invoice, and unrelated later document each fail.
The signer sends the signed record and declaration no later than three days after the act in this procedure. Vendor closure, unsigned summary, or renewal are not relevant.
Only after receipt of the record and declaration does the notary execute the certificate. Neither the presigning nor premailing stages suffice, and the certificate remains required.

The additional statement reports witnessing the named individual sign the attached record and declaration by communication technology on the stated date. Mail receipt, price and in-person visit are not that statement.
The effective date of a compliant remote paper declaration act is declaration signing, not later delivery, renewal, or a recipient's selected date.
The safe harbor does not exclude another method that fulfills the same-record requirement. A vendor cannot waive the condition and the declaration route is not exclusive.

Subject to other Vermont law, identify the individual, record the person taking the oath audiovisually, and retain it. Absence of a document signature, voicemail, and invoices do not remove the requirements.
The certificate must state that communication technology was used. A physical visit would be inaccurate; a lawful remote appearance occurred and equipment brand does not state the method.
Part 7 electronic-record duties apply alongside remote requirements. Identity alone, paper tools, and consent do not remove either set.
Record audiovisual performance simultaneously. A final image or invoice omits the event, and later slideshow reconstruction is not simultaneous.
Current Rule 8-2(f)(i) sets seven years from the act, overriding the statute's express 10-year fallback when no different rule applies. Vendor defaults, three months and download do not override it.

The deceased notary's personal representative is named. Guardians, conservators, agents, and properly designated repositories may also have roles, while a customer or stranger with access does not acquire authority and death does not erase the duty.
The notary must physically be in Vermont. Signer location, area code and server geography cannot replace physical presence.
Where the overseas signer is located, the act must not be prohibited. A U.S. mailing address or waiver does not cure this and Vermont's rule requires examining foreign law.
U.S. government/entity, property, or substantial transaction nexus is required (in addition to the separate foreign prohibition condition). Notary preference or webcam does not supply nexus.
Puerto Rico is expressly within the domestic area for the definition. Statehood, citizenship and billing currency are not this geographic test.
Simultaneous, uninterrupted, real-time sight and sound throughout the act includes identity proofing, signing and notarial execution. Early audio, later email or one visible side falls short.
Technology must facilitate vision, hearing or speech impairments. Pricing, advertising and support only for unimpaired participants do not meet the requirement.
The technology must permit clear viewing, reading and recording the front and back of the presented ID. Neither typed initials nor avatars substitute, and the back is included.
Authentication reasonably limiting access to authorized parties is the required feature. A public invitation would defeat it, and monitor size or slogans do not authenticate.
Reasonable safeguards prevent unauthorized access to live communications, recordings, credential/verification methods, and electronic records. Coverage of calls, titles or marketing only fails.

Technology must produce recordings to the notary, OPR, a court or investigating law enforcement upon the relevant request. Deletion, vendor-only viewing or static marketing images cannot provide that.
Credential analysis uses automated assistance and tests relevant visual, physical or cryptographic security features. No popularity rating, declaration or email spelling supplies authenticity.

Confirm personal and credential details from available issuer or authoritative information consistent with sound commercial practices. Nicknames, advertisements and payment amounts do not supply such a source.
Notary must be able to compare information and photo on the credential against the live individual. Automation does not remove the check and vendor logos or a prior profile are inapposite.
Identity KBA has a five-question minimum tied to personal history or identity. Difficulty, vendor promise and the separate 30-question commission exam do not alter it.
Each KBA item requires five or more options. Timing and four-choice practice items do not modify the rule, and two is below minimum.
At least 80% means four of these five, so three fails. Mere majority and notary discretion do not change it, and 30 pertains to a different exam.
All KBA answers are due within two minutes. Commission cycle, midnight and a vendor-selected period are not the time limit.
The first failed attempt permits one retake within 24 hours, not five attempts, no retake or unlimited ones.
At least 40% of the original questions must be replaced; two of five meets the floor. Thirty is a different exam count, one is 20%, and consent cannot waive it.
After failing a second time, no retake with the same online notary is allowed within 24 hours of the second failure. Unlimited retries, payment, or the signer holding a commission do not change it.
The notary cannot see or record the KBA questions or answers. Photography, sale, and saving even after a tip all fail.
Storage, communications and identity proofing providers must register to do business in Vermont with the Secretary of State. Customer citizenship or a private award cannot replace registration.
Communications or proofing providers must demonstrate their capability to the notary's satisfaction. Customer warranty, discount, or a slogan does not establish compliance.

The 10-year statute defaults only if no rule sets another period; current rule specifies at least seven years. Neither blanket rejection of the rule, an exam timing interpretation, nor vendor discretion works.
Fixed two-year periods and printed expiration dates control, not an issue-date anniversary, lifetime status, or stamp vendor.
Midnight at the end of the expiration date ends unrenewed credentials. Customer appointments, ink, or a supposed courtesy extension do not keep them active.
Nonreceipt of a courtesy renewal email leaves the continuous-maintenance duty unchanged. Calls, reminder delivery or customer knowledge do not extend authority.

Initial credential issued in the last 90 days carries through the next full biennial period without intervening renewal, fees or CE. Future cycles remain subject to renewal and issuing a commission does not confer a lifetime endorsement.
Late renewal is subject to reinstatement penalty fees and online waiver requests. Waiver is not automatic, fees are not owed to customers, and lateness does have consequences.
OPR's February 2026 public instructions open renewal six weeks beforehand. Daily availability, a broken stamp or waiting until expiration do not describe the window.

Replace unsupported age characterization of a discrepancy still present on the May 2026 public exam form. Scope to current ordinary commission renewal, specify the relevant period and exemptions, and preserve B. This is a site wording correction; current requirements are unchanged.
